summary: A small white wooden tower on a concrete pier at the end of a sand spit, marking the mouth of Shelburne Harbour since 1873 (present tower 1880).

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed; reachable on foot across the sandbar at low tide only.

notes_for_editor: Keeper roster and 1873/1880 report details rest on Lighthouse Friends (secondary; it quotes the Department annual reports, which are not in the local corpus before 1900). Not verified against the 1873/1880 reports, nor the keeper dates. Disagreement on the post-1980 status: Canadian Register says decommissioned 1999; Lighthouse Friends says discontinued 1996; Lighthouse Directory says inactive 1996-2008 then reactivated; Coast Guard list shows a private aid, F R, 14.3 m, 6 nm. The 1904 report volume's text is OCR (the 17 feet reads 'I 7'). Ownership: Lighthouse Friends says Sandy Point Community Recreation Group, Lighthouse Directory says National Lighthouse Trust owner. Annual-report keeper tables for the Sand Spit station appear in the corpus (1900-1910) but are column-misaligned and were not used. The SaltWire article is undated in the cached text. Checker: the 2001 federal heritage event was removed (no year in the cached source 3). Stevens 'Stephens' variant note removed (tables not read). The 1904 report is for fiscal year ended 30 June 1904, p.35-36 confirmed by page index.
